context.egyptFoodExports: Egypt food exports $4.607B in the 2025 reporting window (FEC; article says first eight months), +9%; top destinations Saudi $356M, USA $304M, Sudan $241M, Libya $204M, Jordan $186M, Iraq $152M, UAE $151M, Algeria $143M, Lebanon $141M (egypttoday.com). Egypt chocolate exports 2025 $251M (+64%): Saudi ~$87M, UAE $37M, Kuwait ~$18M, UK ~$15M, Qatar $12M (dailynewsegypt.com).
context.hormuz: Iran war since 28 Feb 2026; Strait of Hormuz effectively closed (day 222 on 8 Oct 2026, ~5% of normal transits per IMF PortWatch via straits.live). Gulf-side ports (Kuwait, Qatar, UAE Jebel Ali, Bahrain, southern Iraq) disrupted; Saudi Red Sea ports, Jordan/Aqaba and Oman's outside-strait ports are the workable entry points. Favours Dr. Baker's Madinah plant and Egyptian Red Sea/Aqaba routes.
context.dataCaveats: Comtrade preview API worked only for Egypt's 2024 exports to a few partners and was not used in the final table; all Egypt export figures are TradingEconomics 2025. World-import figures are 2023 TrendEconomy (Comtrade mirror) at HS4; no 6-digit 040130 cream data found for any country. Libya/Iraq/Algeria import data are stale or missing.

recommendation: Ranking rationale: (1) Saudi Arabia - INCREASE: biggest import pool, Egypt already #1 in chocolate, Madinah factory + Saudi distributors, Red Sea ports unaffected by Hormuz closure; push dairy/cream systems, fillings and spreads through Foodex Saudi (16-18 Nov). (2) UAE - ENTER as showcase and re-export hub through Gulfood Manufacturing (3-5 Nov); highest pay safety but crowded and sea logistics disrupted, so supply via Saudi land bridge/Fujairah. (3) Jordan - INCREASE: proven Egyptian outlet ($744M), Agadir+GAFTA, Aqaba route avoids Hormuz and serves Iraq/Levant; watch Jordan label/powdered-milk licensing. (4) Kenya - ENTER: COMESA FTA, Egypt already #1 in chocolate, EAC gateway; approach via Africa Food Show contacts. (5) Kuwait - INCREASE only via Saudi land corridor and local PAFN-registered importer; Egypt already #1 chocolate supplier. WATCH: Qatar and Oman (small pools, logistics), Iraq (Erbil fair 23-26 Nov, high risk), Libya and Ethiopia (payment/FX), Algeria (opaque import controls), Nigeria (largest gap, FX/NAFDAC), Tunisia, Ghana (small pools).
